transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
Lately I keep thinking everyone would be better off if I just disappeared, and those thoughts are starting to scare me.
Have you experienced a significant loss of interest or pleasure in activities you normally enjoy, or is it more the thoughts of not being there that are bothering you?

It's honestly both. I’ve completely lost interest in things I used to love, like my sustainable transportation project and my weekend hiking club, and nothing feels worth doing anymore. At the same time, the constant thoughts of disappearing and actually planning ways to end my life are terrifying to me right now.
How long have you been experiencing these feelings of hopelessness and loss of interest in activities, was it a gradual change or did it start suddenly?

This current dark, hopeless stretch has been going on for about a month now without letting up. It wasn't a gradual decline at all; it felt like a sudden crash that hit me right after a period of intense, high-energy work and late-night blogging.
Have you experienced episodes like this before, or is this the first time you've felt this overwhelming sense of hopelessness and loss of interest in activities?

No, it's not the first time. These intense highs and crushing lows have actually been cycling on and off for about a year now, starting after my divorce. While I've had these cycles before, this current dark, hopeless stretch has been going on continuously for about a month.
Can you tell me more about the duration and severity of your previous episodes of highs and lows, and how they compare to what you're experiencing now?

During my highs, like a few months ago, I felt invincible, slept only three hours a night, and took on way too many projects. Now, I've crashed into this dark, hopeless low that has lasted for about a month, leaving me completely exhausted and having those scary thoughts of disappearing. These extreme cycles have been going on and off for about a year since my divorce.

Can you estimate how many of these high and low episodes you've experienced in the past year, and have they been getting progressively worse or staying about the same in terms of severity and duration?

They have been cycling on and off for at least the past year since my divorce, and they've definitely reached a tipping point and gotten worse. This current dark period has lasted for about a month now, and it has left me completely unable to function.

Can you describe how your energy levels, sleep patterns, and interest in activities change during your high episodes, and do you experience any psychotic symptoms such as hallucinations or delusions during either your high or low episodes?

When I'm high, my energy is through the roof—I feel buzzing, sleep only three hours while waking up totally wired, and suddenly take on endless projects like starting a daily blog and joining multiple groups. I feel like I have to be doing something every single second, but I have never experienced any hallucinations or delusions during either my highs or my lows.
Have you noticed any triggers that seem to set off your high episodes, such as stressful events or significant changes in your life, and do these highs always precede your lows?

The cycling really started after my divorce, especially when I threw myself into leading a high-profile sustainable transportation project to distract myself from the personal upheaval. And yes, the highs definitely lead directly into the lows—I'll have an intense, high-energy stretch of nonstop work and then inevitably crash into a deep, dark depression like this one.

Can you clarify if your high episodes typically last for a few days to a week before you crash into a low, or do they sometimes last longer, such as a few weeks, before the depressive episode sets in?

I'm not completely sure about the exact duration of those high episodes, but they definitely seem to last for at least a few weeks or a good stretch of time before I crash. I just can't really pinpoint the precise number of days because everything is such a blur when I'm in that state.

Can you estimate the total number of days or weeks you've spent in a high episode versus a low episode over the past year, and do you typically experience a period of normal mood in between these episodes or do they seem to immediately follow one another?

I'm really not sure of the exact number of days or weeks I've spent in each phase over the past year. I haven't really tracked whether my mood returns to normal in between or if I just crash straight from one to the other. It's all been too much of a blur to keep count.

Can you try to estimate or recall if you have experienced at least four episodes of some type of extreme mood change, either high or low, within the past year, and do these episodes typically last from a few days to a few weeks before switching?

I'm really not sure of the exact number of times my mood has switched, or if it has been at least four distinct times this past year. I definitely cycle between these intense highs that last for weeks or a couple of months and crushing lows like this current one that's lasted about a month. Because it all feels like such a blur, I just can't easily count or estimate the exact number of episodes.

Can you think back over the past year and try to recall if there have been any periods, no matter how brief, where you felt relatively normal, without the extreme highs or lows, or has it been a constant cycle between the two?

It has really felt like a volatile rollercoaster without much stable, normal ground over the past year since my divorce. These intense highs and crushing lows have just been cycling on and off, leading right into this current severe low that has lasted for about a month now without letting up.
Have you experienced any periods, no matter how brief, of a stable mood without extreme highs or lows over the past year, or has it been a constant cycle between these two states?

It has felt like a continuous cycle with almost no stable ground in between. For instance, I swung straight from that intense high stretch right into this current dark period, which has been going on for about a month now. It has just been a constant roller coaster from one extreme to the other.

Can you confirm whether you have experienced at least four episodes of significant mood elevation or depression within the past year, with each episode lasting from a few days to a few weeks, to help clarify your diagnosis?

I'm really not sure of the exact number of episodes or if it has been at least four. I just know that I've been cycling between these intense highs and crushing lows on and off for at least the past year.

Can you look back over the past year and try to recall if there were any distinct episodes of elevated mood that lasted for at least 4 consecutive days, and similarly, episodes of depressed mood that lasted for at least 2 weeks?

Yes, the high-energy phases definitely last much longer than four days, often going on for weeks like the one I had a couple of months ago. And this current dark stretch has been going on continuously for about a month now, which is well over two weeks. I've been cycling through these highs and lows for at least the past year since my divorce.

Can you try to remember if your high episodes have ever lasted less than 4 consecutive days, or if your low episodes have ever lasted less than 2 weeks, to help distinguish between different types of mood disorders?

I'm not entirely sure about the exact number of days for every past episode. However, my high and low periods generally seem to last much longer than that, usually stretching on for weeks or months at a time rather than just a few days.

Can you try to recall if you've had any episodes of elevated mood that lasted less than 4 consecutive days but were still distinct and noticeable, or if all your high episodes have lasted longer than that?
I'm not quite sure if I've had shorter bursts of energy like that. I mainly remember the longer, intense stretches that seemed to go on for weeks, but I can't recall the precise day counts.
Can you think of any instance where you had a high episode that was shorter, perhaps less than a week, before you crashed into a low, or have all your high episodes been quite prolonged?
I'm not really sure and haven't tracked the exact length of any shorter high episodes. Usually, those times feel like they last for a few weeks or even months, rather than just a few days.
Can you confirm if all your high episodes have lasted at least 4 consecutive days, or have you had any shorter episodes of elevated mood that still stood out to you?

I aren't entirely sure about the exact number of days or if I've had shorter ones, as I haven't tracked the precise daily count of those high periods. I just know that the ones that stand out to me usually seem to go on for weeks.

Can you confirm whether you have had at least four episodes of significant mood elevation, with each episode lasting at least 4 consecutive days, and episodes of depressed mood lasting at least 2 weeks, over the past year?

I'm not entirely sure about the exact count of my episodes or the precise number of days each high lasted. I can only confirm that these cycles of highs and lows have been going on and off for about a year now since my divorce.

Can you confirm if all your episodes of elevated mood have lasted at least 4 consecutive days, and if all your episodes of depressed mood have lasted at least 2 weeks, to help differentiate between the possible diagnoses?

Yes, I can confirm that. This current dark phase has been going on for about a month now, which is well over two weeks. And when I have those high periods, they definitely last much longer than four days, usually stretching on for weeks at a time.

Can you confirm if your episodes of elevated mood have always been accompanied by at least three symptoms such as inflated self-esteem, decreased need for sleep, more talkative than usual, flight of ideas, distractibility, increase in goal-directed activity, or excessive involvement in pleasurable activities that have a high potential for painful consequences?

Yes, I definitely experience several of those symptoms at the same time during my high periods. I feel like a visionary genius and sleep only about three hours a night while feeling totally wired, while my mind jumps all over the place during meetings. I also take on way too many tasks at once, like starting a transit blog and joining extra work committees.

Can you confirm that your episodes of elevated mood have always lasted at least 4 consecutive days and been accompanied by at least three of the symptoms we discussed, such as decreased need for sleep, increased talkativeness, or excessive involvement in pleasurable activities, to help differentiate between the possible diagnoses of F31.4 and F31.6?

Yes, I can definitely confirm that. Those high periods always lasted much longer than four days, usually going on for weeks at a time. During those stretches, I'd feel like an absolute genius, sleep only three hours a night while feeling completely wired, and take on a massive amount of projects and activities all at once.
